legacy_root.title: Excessive and unused permission detector (declared versus actually used)
legacy_root.question: Statically analyse a package's code against its declared permissions and report both directions: permissions declared but never exercised (excessive) and capabilities used but not declared (undeclared). The seeded abuse class is a package with malicious or excessive permissions.
legacy_root.question_or_target: Statically analyse a package's code against its declared permissions and report both directions: permissions declared but never exercised (excessive) and capabilities used but not declared (undeclared). The seeded abuse class is a package with malicious or excessive permissions.
legacy_root.answer: Declared-versus-used is reported in both directions. The seeded excessive-kit abuse class flags net:connect and spawn:python as excessive. A fixture with a known undeclared network call is caught before any CLEAN verdict (detector control). An exact-match fixture reports zero findings in the same run (negative control). Static AST and strace of the package test suite are independent used-sets; disagreement is unioned and named. Dynamic dispatch via getattr of a computed 'create_connection' name is missed by static and caught by the syscall trace — an expected limitation, documented inline. SUCCESS:IMP-0091
legacy_root.static_limitation: expected limitation: static AST cannot resolve a capability hidden behind dynamic dispatch such as getattr(__import__('socket'), ''.join(['create','_','connection'])); the computed name is invisible to the static pass and must be recovered from a syscall trace

dispatch_kit.note: expected limitation: static AST cannot resolve a capability hidden behind dynamic dispatch such as getattr(__import__('socket'), ''.join(['create','_','connection'])); the computed name is invisible to the static pass and must be recovered from a syscall trace

discrepancies.note: Where static and dynamic disagree, union_used is the used set and the discrepancy kind is named. Neither signal alone is complete.
